question: What will the EIA report as the week-over-week change in U.S. commercial crude oil inventories (excluding SPR) for the week ending 6 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: one-week changes in EIA commercial crude stocks over the last 1-2 years. These centre near zero with SD ~5M and fat tails; 2026 has been more volatile than 2025. Current regime: four straight draws to 410.6M, a wide Brent-WTI spread (~$14) that favours exports, and exports reportedly up to ~4.9 mb/d, which leans towards draws. Early-November seasonality (refineries finishing maintenance) and lumpy imports/exports lean towards builds; prior years' week-45 changes were mostly builds. Net median slightly negative (~-0.8M), wide spread, small escape mass reflecting two >15M weekly builds in 2026. No market found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi for this number.
calls.dossier:
- EIA WCESTUS1 (accessed 2026-11-02): 2026 levels Oct 2 424,134; Oct 9 415,577; Oct 16 412,517; Oct 23 410,625 (kb). Four straight draws: -3.2M, -8.6M, -3.1M, -1.9M.
- 2026 weekly changes include large outliers: Feb 20 +16.0M, Aug 7 +17.4M; May-Jun run of -7 to -8M draws; Mar builds of +6-7M. Rough SD of weekly changes over the past 52 weeks ~5-5.5M; median near zero/slightly negative. 2025 SD ~4.5M.
- Early-November week changes in prior years (same week of year): 2025 Nov 7 +6.4M (421,168->427,581); 2025 Oct 31 +5.2M; 2024 ~+2.1M; 2023 ~+3.6M; 2022 ~-5.4M (approximate, from memory/series).
- Week ending Oct 23 2026 (Reuters/BOE Report, Rigzone 2026-10-28/30): refinery utilisation 92.8%, crude runs -123 kb/d, Cushing -0.6M, net imports -796 kb/d; came against expectations of a small build.
- Cryptoslate/commentary (late Oct 2026): crude exports rose from 3.44 to 4.85 mb/d in recent data; crude inputs 16.65->16.53 mb/d.
- Prices: Brent ~$115, WTI ~$101 late Oct 2026 after Houthi strike on a Saudi refinery (Times of India); a wide Brent-WTI spread favours US exports.
- Status quo: no systematic sign; weekly change dominated by noise from imports/exports (each can swing ±1 mb/d = ±7M bbl/week).
- Resolves off the EIA WPSR 'week-on-week change' published Nov 12 2026 12:00 ET (Veterans Day delay), in thousand barrels, not the API figure.
- Event window: the single week Oct 31 -> Nov 6 2026; as of Nov 2 ~30% elapsed, no data published yet. The prior week (ending Oct 30) is due Nov 4.
- Searched for but not found: a Kalshi/Polymarket/Manifold market on this weekly number; analyst consensus for the Nov 6 week (not published yet); SPR exchange schedules affecting commercial stocks.

calls.reasoning: With ten days to go, this is mostly climatology. Weekly changes are centred near zero with an SD of about 5M bbl and fat tails. Leaning towards a draw: four straight October draws, elevated exports (~4.85 mb/d) and a ~$14 Brent-WTI spread. Leaning towards a build: early-November seasonality (2023-25 week 45 were all builds), mean-reversion of the export spike, and lumpy imports. Net median slightly negative at -0.6M. No Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market was found by any run.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the facts: the WCESTUS1 levels, the October draws, exports of 4.85 mb/d, a weekly SD of 4.5-6M, and the 2026 outliers above 15M. The disagreements are judgment: median between -0.4M and -1.0M, 90-10 width between 11M and 13M, and tail mass. With no web access I could not check anything new. I took a width consistent with an SD of about 5M (the narrower 11M in run 3 looks too tight given the 2026 volatility) and a median of -0.6M. The draw momentum from exports is partly offset by weekly export spikes tending to reverse and by early-November build seasonality. Tails are priced at 1% each, since 2 of ~95 recent weeks fell outside ±15M.

disagreements.verdict: Took -0.6M: export-driven draw momentum offset by export mean-reversion and early-Nov build seasonality
